title: Multi-Agent Systems: When More Agents Help
summary: Splitting work across several agents can cut latency and keep each context small, but it adds coordination cost and new ways to fail. This lesson quantifies when it pays, where errors spread, and how to design handoffs.
objectives: After this lesson you can describe the common multi-agent shapes: orchestrator with sub-agents, pipeline, peer review and debate
Compute the latency speedup and the token effect of running specialists in parallel with isolated contexts
Count communication channels for hub-and-spoke versus fully connected designs
Estimate how handoff loss and unverified outputs compound error across agents
Decide, with an expected-value comparison, whether a multi-agent design is worth its extra cost
prerequisites: Workflow patterns and compounding reliability from [/learn/agents/workflows-vs-agents](/learn/agents/workflows-vs-agents), context growth from [/learn/agents/agent-loop](/learn/agents/agent-loop), and state and memory from [/learn/agents/memory-and-state](/learn/agents/memory-and-state).
